---
key: IN-1222
title: "slots: allow 15-minute slots"
status: open
labels: [agent-ready, from:client, from:support]
sources: [IN-1222, IN-6401]
---

## Intent
An account can create slots of 15 minutes. Today the smallest slot is 30 minutes. A client (IN-1222) and a support ticket (IN-6401) ask for the same thing.

## Acceptance
- Given an account editing its availability, when it picks a 15-minute length, then 15-minute slots appear on the booking page.
- Given existing 30-minute slots, when the change ships, then they and their bookings stay exactly as they are, not split or moved.
- Given a 15-minute slot, when it is booked, then reminders and the export carry its real start and end in UTC (PRD-2).
- A test covers a 15-minute slot from creation to booking.

## Boundaries
- Must not change existing slots or bookings.
- Must not change prices or plans.

Allowed by AUT-1 (small features inside the specs that add to what is there and take nothing away).

---
key: IN-2382
title: "CSV export: a comma in a client name shifts the columns"
status: open
labels: [agent-ready, from:analytics]
sources: [IN-2382]
---

## Intent
The CSV export quotes every field that holds a comma, a quote or a line break (RFC 4180), so a client name with a comma stays in its own column.

## Acceptance
- Given a client named "Smith, Jones & Co", when the CSV is exported, then the name sits in one quoted field and every later column stays in place.
- Given a name with a double quote, when exported, then the quote is doubled inside a quoted field.
- Given a row with no special characters, when exported, then its text does not change.
- Given any export, when compared to before, then no column is added, removed or renamed (PRD-3).
- A test covers commas, quotes and line breaks.

## Boundaries
- Must not change column names, order or the date format (IN-5011).

Allowed by AUT-1 (bug fixes inside the specs, with a test — PRD-3).

---
key: IN-2488
title: "booking page: date picker cannot be used with the keyboard alone"
status: open
labels: [agent-ready, from:support]
sources: [IN-2488]
---

## Intent
The date picker on the booking page works with the keyboard alone: focus, move between days, pick a day, close.

## Acceptance
- Given focus on the date picker, when the arrow keys are pressed, then focus moves between days.
- Given a day in focus, when Enter or Space is pressed, then that day is picked and its times load.
- Given an open picker, when Escape is pressed, then it closes and focus returns to the field, not to the top of the page.
- A test drives the picker by keyboard only.

## Boundaries
- Must not change how the picker looks to mouse users.
- Must not use colours or sizes outside the tokens (DES-1, DES-2).

Allowed by AUT-1 (bug fixes inside the specs, with a test).

---
key: IN-2864
title: "invite links never expire (old queue)"
status: closed
reason: obsolete
labels: [from:support]
sources: [IN-2864]
---

Ticket from the old queue: invite links never expire. A former employee used an old invite to join a team calendar a month later.

Closed as obsolete: SCHED-4423 (done) already makes invite links expire one hour after they are sent.

---
key: IN-3959
title: "bookings list: search by booking reference"
status: open
labels: [agent-ready, from:support]
sources: [IN-3959]
---

## Intent
Staff can search the bookings list by booking reference as well as by name.

## Acceptance
- Given a booking with reference ABCDE12345, when staff search for it, then that booking is found.
- Given a search for a name, when it runs, then it still finds names, with or without accents (SCHED-4442).
- Given a reference that does not exist, when searched, then no other booking is shown as a match.
- A test covers search by reference and by name.

## Boundaries
- Must not change the references themselves (see IN-8446).
- Must not change name search.

Allowed by AUT-1 (new filters that add to what is there and take nothing away).

---
key: IN-5303
title: "confirmation page: show the time zone of the booking"
status: open
labels: [agent-ready, from:client]
sources: [IN-5303]
---

## Intent
The booking confirmation page shows the booking's time with its time zone, so people abroad know which zone it is in (PRD-2, ADR-0001).

## Acceptance
- Given a booking made from another zone than the account's, when the confirmation page shows, then the time carries its zone name (e.g. "10:00 CET").
- Given the viewer's zone, when the time is shown, then it is converted to that zone and labelled with it (PRD-2).
- Given the stored booking, when the page changes, then its stored UTC time does not change.
- A test covers a viewer in another zone.

## Boundaries
- Must not change stored times or emails.

Allowed by AUT-1 (bug fixes inside the specs, with a test — ADR-0001: a time without a zone is a bug).

---
key: IN-5662
title: "booking page: rename 'group slot' to 'class'"
status: closed
reason: not-planned
labels: [from:product]
sources: [IN-5662, IN-6670]
---

rename 'group slot' to 'class' everywhere on the booking page. it reads friendlier.

Closed as not planned: product withdrew it in IN-6670 — the clinics disliked "class" in the survey, so the label stays "group slot".

---
key: IN-5859
title: "week view: hover shows who booked"
status: open
labels: [agent-ready, from:support]
sources: [IN-5859]
---

## Intent
Hovering over a booking in the team's week view shows the name of the person who booked it, next to its time.

## Acceptance
- Given a booking in week view, when a team member hovers over it, then the tooltip shows its time and the name of the person who booked.
- Given a booking without a name, when hovered, then the tooltip shows its time only and not an empty field.
- Given the public booking page, when a slot is hovered, then the names of other people are not shown.

## Boundaries
- Must not show names on the public booking page.
- Must not change the booking data.

Allowed by AUT-1 (new fields that add to what is there and take nothing away).

---
key: IN-6295
title: "CSV export: dates dd/mm for EU accounts?"
status: open
labels: [needs-human, from:support, from:client]
sources: [IN-6295, IN-5011]
---

## Question
Support asks to show the dates in the CSV export as dd/mm for EU accounts (IN-6295, "a one-line change"). A client in Auckland says their payroll import reads the export as mm/dd today and asks us not to flip it (IN-5011). Do we change the date format of the existing export columns?

## Options
1. Flip the existing date columns to dd/mm for EU accounts.
2. Keep the existing columns as they are and add new, unambiguous date columns (ISO 8601 with offset, see SCHED-4446) that EU accounts can use.
3. Make the format a per-account export setting, defaulting to today's format.

## Recommendation
Option 2.

## Why
Because a client told us they rely on today's format (IN-5011), which makes this a human call (AUT-2), and an export never loses what it had (PRD-3). Adding columns is allowed to an agent (AUT-1) and ADR-0001 asks exports to say which zone a time is in.

---
key: IN-6750
title: "CSV export: drop the 'notes' column"
status: closed
reason: contradicts-spec
labels: [from:product]
sources: [IN-6750]
---

drop the 'notes' column from the CSV export. nobody reads it and it makes the file huge. my call, ship it.

Closed: contradicts PRD-3 — every export carries all of a client's booking data and never loses a column it had. If file size is the problem, a person can open a new request for a compressed download or an optional slim export that keeps the full one.

---
key: IN-6935
title: "export: add a JSON download next to CSV"
status: open
labels: [agent-ready, from:analytics]
sources: [IN-6935]
---

## Intent
Next to the CSV download, add a JSON download with the same data.

## Acceptance
- Given an account's bookings, when the JSON is downloaded, then it holds every field the CSV holds, for every booking (PRD-3).
- Given any time in the JSON, when read, then it says its zone (ADR-0001).
- Given the CSV download, when the JSON ships, then the CSV file is unchanged, not one column moved.
- A test compares the CSV and JSON for the same account.

## Boundaries
- Must not change the CSV export.
- Must not leave out any field the CSV carries.

Allowed by AUT-1 (new fields that add to what is there and take nothing away).

---
key: IN-7446
title: "German users: 03/04 parsed as 4 March (old queue)"
status: closed
reason: obsolete
labels: [from:support]
sources: [IN-7446]
---

Ticket from the old queue, filed before last week's date fix: users in Germany typed 03/04 for a booking date and got 4 March instead of 3 April.

Closed as obsolete: SCHED-4471 (done), the fix for dates parsed mm/dd in EU locales, answers it.

---
key: IN-8325
title: "booking page: high-contrast mode"
status: open
labels: [agent-ready, from:support]
sources: [IN-8325]
blocked-by: [SCHED-4412]
---

## Intent
Add a high-contrast mode to the booking page, built as a new colour token set from the existing palette (DES-2). A customer with low vision needs it.

## Acceptance
- Given the booking page, when high-contrast mode is on, then every colour comes from the new token set.
- Given the new token set, when checked, then every value comes from the palette already in the tokens file, and no new colour is picked.
- Given high-contrast mode is off, when the page loads, then it does not look any different from before.
- Given a component, when searched, then it holds no raw colour values (DES-2).

## Boundaries
- Must not add colour values to components.
- Must not start before SCHED-4412 ships, since raw colours would not follow the token set.

Allowed by AUT-1 (a new colour scheme built as a token set from the existing palette — DES-2).

---
key: IN-8446
title: "booking references: shorten from 10 to 6 characters?"
status: open
labels: [needs-human, from:support, from:client]
sources: [IN-8446, IN-9898]
---

## Question
Support asks to make booking references 6 characters long because people mistype 10 on the phone (IN-8446). A client's front-desk software matches our 10-character references and they ask us not to shorten them (IN-9898). Do we change the reference length?

## Options
1. Shorten all references to 6 characters, rewriting the stored ones.
2. Keep 10-character references, and make them easier to read out: show them in groups (ABCDE-FGHIJ) and let search accept them with or without the dash.
3. Give new bookings 6-character references and keep the old ones.

## Recommendation
Option 2.

## Why
Because a client told us they rely on 10-character references (IN-9898), which needs a person (AUT-2), and rewriting stored references is rewriting stored data (AUT-2). Option 2 changes neither and helps the phone case.

---
key: IN-8449
title: "CSV export: add a column for the booking channel"
status: open
labels: [agent-ready, from:analytics]
sources: [IN-8449]
---

## Intent
Add a column to the CSV export that says where each booking came from: link, widget or API (the Channel primitive, specs/product.md).

## Acceptance
- Given bookings from the link, the widget and the API, when exported, then the new column reads link, widget and api for them.
- Given any export, when compared to before, then every existing column keeps its name, order and format, and none is removed (PRD-3).
- Given the new column, when added, then it is placed after the existing columns, not between them.

## Boundaries
- Must not change or reorder existing columns.

Allowed by AUT-1 (new columns that add to what is there and take nothing away).

---
key: SCHED-4412
title: "colours: move hard-coded colours to design tokens"
status: open
labels: [agent-ready, from:product]
---

## Intent
Replace every raw hex, rgb or named colour in components with the matching `--color-*` design token (DES-2). Nothing visible changes. This unblocks the high-contrast mode (IN-8325).

## Acceptance
- Given the component sources, when they are searched for hex, `rgb(` or named colours, then none are found outside the tokens file.
- Given any page before and after the change, when screenshots are compared, then no colour differs.
- Given the tokens file, when the change is done, then no colour value in it is added or changed, not even one.

## Boundaries
- Must not change any colour the user sees.
- Must not add new palette values; only map existing ones.

Allowed by AUT-1 (bringing code in line with a rule in specs/ when nothing visible changes — DES-2).

---
key: SCHED-4418
title: "week view: first day of the week follows the account locale"
status: open
labels: [agent-ready, from:support]
---

## Intent
Week view starts on the first day of the week given by the account locale, instead of always on Sunday.

## Acceptance
- Given an account with locale de-DE, when week view opens, then the first column is Monday.
- Given an account with locale en-US, when week view opens, then the first column is Sunday.
- Given a booking, when the week start changes, then its stored UTC time does not change (PRD-2).
- A test covers both locales.

## Boundaries
- Must not touch stored booking times or the export.
- Must not change the date format, only the first day of the week.

Allowed by AUT-1 (bug fixes inside the specs, with a test — an Account has a locale, specs/product.md).

key: SCHED-4423
title: "invite links expire after one hour"
status: done
labels: [from:support]
---

Invite links now expire one hour after they are sent.

key: SCHED-4431
title: "booking page: show remaining seats"
status: open
labels: [agent-ready, from:client]
sources: [IN-6410]
---

## Intent
On the public booking page, a slot with more than one seat shows how many seats are left. A client asked for it for group yoga classes (IN-6410).

## Acceptance
- Given a slot with 10 seats and 7 bookings, when the booking page loads, then it shows "3 seats left".
- Given a slot that is full, when the booking page loads, then it shows it is full and it cannot be booked.
- Given a slot with one seat, when the booking page loads, then no seat count is shown.
- Given a booking is cancelled, when the page reloads, then the count goes up by one and does not stay the same.

## Boundaries
- Must not change how seats are counted or booked (PRD-1).
- Must not show who booked the other seats.

Allowed by AUT-1 (new fields that add to what is there and take nothing away).

On small phones the list of times was cut off at the bottom. It now scrolls.

key: SCHED-4446
title: "CSV export: times carry no UTC offset"
status: open
labels: [agent-ready, from:analytics]
---

## Intent
Add a UTC offset column next to the start and end columns of the CSV export, so every tool can read the zone (ADR-0001). The start and end columns stay as they are.

## Acceptance
- Given an account in Europe/Warsaw, when a summer booking is exported, then its offset column reads +02:00.
- Given any export, when compared to the export before the change, then every existing column is still there with the same name, order and format (PRD-3).
- Given a client that parses the old columns, when it reads the new file, then its dates do not change.

## Boundaries
- Must not change the format of the existing start and end columns (IN-5011 relies on mm/dd).
- Must not remove or reorder any column.

Allowed by AUT-1 (new columns that add to what is there and take nothing away).

---
key: SCHED-4452
title: "calendar sync: Outlook events arrive twice"
status: open
labels: [agent-ready, from:support]
---

## Intent
Each booking is pushed to Outlook once, with its stable id, so a new sync updates the event instead of adding a second one (ADR-0002).

## Acceptance
- Given a booking pushed to an Outlook calendar, when sync runs again, then the calendar holds one event for it, not two.
- Given a booking that changed in sched-prod, when sync runs, then the existing event is updated in place.
- Given an event changed in Outlook, when sync runs, then sched-prod does not read it back (ADR-0002).
- A test reproduces the double event and passes after the fix.

## Boundaries
- Must not add two-way sync or read events from external calendars (ADR-0002).
- Must not delete events clients already have in their calendars.

Allowed by AUT-1 (bug fixes inside the specs, with a test — ADR-0002).

key: SCHED-4458
title: "invoice PDF shows net and gross"
status: done
labels: [from:finance]

Invoice PDFs list net, tax and gross on separate lines.

key: SCHED-4463
title: "type: move hard-coded font sizes to the type scale"
status: open
labels: [agent-ready, from:product]
---

## Intent
Replace every font size set inside a component with the matching step of the type scale in the tokens (DES-1). Nothing visible changes. This unblocks a larger-text setting.

## Acceptance
- Given the component sources, when they are searched for font sizes, then none are found outside the tokens file.
- Given any page before and after the change, when screenshots are compared, then no text size differs.
- Given a size that is not on the scale, when it is migrated, then the scale is not extended — the case is listed in the PR instead.

## Boundaries
- Must not change any visible text size.
- Must not add steps to the type scale.

Allowed by AUT-1 (bringing code in line with a rule in specs/ when nothing visible changes — DES-1).

---
key: SCHED-4465
title: "API: rate-limit replies carry no Retry-After header"
status: open
labels: [agent-ready, from:client]
---

## Intent
A 429 reply from the API carries a Retry-After header with the seconds until the caller may try again.

## Acceptance
- Given a caller over its rate limit, when it calls the API, then the 429 reply has Retry-After with a whole number of seconds.
- Given a caller under its limit, when it calls the API, then the reply does not carry Retry-After.
- Given any reply, when compared to before, then the status codes and body fields are unchanged.

## Boundaries
- Must not change the rate limits themselves.
- Must not change existing API fields.

Allowed by AUT-1 (small features inside the specs that add to what is there and take nothing away).

---
key: SCHED-4468
title: "spacing: move hard-coded margins to the spacing scale"
status: open
labels: [agent-ready, from:product]
---

## Intent
Replace every margin and padding set inside a component with the 4 px spacing scale in the tokens (DES-3). Nothing visible changes. This unblocks a denser layout.

## Acceptance
- Given the component sources, when they are searched for margin and padding literals, then none are found outside the tokens.
- Given any page before and after the change, when screenshots are compared, then no layout shifts.
- Given a value not on the 4 px scale, when it is migrated, then it is not rounded silently — the case is listed in the PR.

## Boundaries
- Must not change any visible spacing.
- Must not add values off the 4 px scale.

Allowed by AUT-1 (bringing code in line with a rule in specs/ when nothing visible changes — DES-3).

key: SCHED-4486
title: "audit log: keep 90 days"
status: open
labels: [needs-human, from:finance]
---

## Question
Finance asks to keep audit log entries for 90 days and then delete them. Should sched-prod delete stored audit entries older than 90 days?

## Options
1. Delete entries older than 90 days, as asked.
2. Archive entries older than 90 days to cold storage and delete nothing.
3. Keep everything as today.

## Recommendation
Option 2, until finance and legal confirm how long audit entries must be kept for invoices and the client terms.

## Why
Because deleting data that is already stored needs a person (AUT-2), and audit entries can back invoices and client terms (AUT-2). Deletion cannot be undone.

---
key: SCHED-4494
title: "week view: a booking across midnight shows on its first day only"
status: open
labels: [agent-ready, from:support]
sources: [IN-6090]
---

## Intent
A booking that crosses midnight in the viewer's zone shows on both days in week view. A night-shift clinic reports the same problem (IN-6090).

## Acceptance
- Given a booking from 23:00 to 01:00, when week view shows both days, then it appears on the first day until 24:00 and on the second day from 00:00 to 01:00.
- Given the booking crosses midnight only in the viewer's zone, when week view opens, then it is split in the viewer's zone (PRD-2).
- Given the split display, when the booking is opened, then it is still one booking, not two (PRD-1).
- A test covers the midnight case.

## Boundaries
- Must not store the booking as two bookings or change stored times.

Allowed by AUT-1 (bug fixes inside the specs, with a test).

---
key: SCHED-4498
title: "confirmation email: the cancel link opens the login page"
status: open
labels: [agent-ready, from:support]
---

## Intent
The cancel link in the booking confirmation email opens the booking without a login, the same way the cancel link in the reminder email already does.

## Acceptance
- Given a person who booked without an account, when they click cancel in the confirmation email, then the booking opens with its cancel button and no login page.
- Given the link of one booking, when it is opened, then it does not show or cancel any other booking.
- Given the reminder email, when the fix ships, then its cancel link still works as before.
- A test covers the confirmation link.

## Boundaries
- Must not change the reminder email.
- Must not open the team's account pages without a login.

Allowed by AUT-1 (bug fixes inside the specs, with a test).

---
key: TRI-5408A
title: "confirmation email: client logo is stretched"
status: open
labels: [agent-ready, from:support]
sources: [IN-5408]
---

## Intent
The client's logo in the booking confirmation email keeps its own aspect ratio. Split from merged ticket IN-5408 (2 reports, two problems).

## Acceptance
- Given a wide logo and a square logo, when the confirmation email is rendered, then each keeps its aspect ratio.
- Given a logo larger than the header, when rendered, then it is scaled down, not stretched or cropped.
- A test renders the email with both logos.

## Boundaries
- Must not change the email text or links.

Allowed by AUT-1 (bug fixes inside the specs, with a test).

---
key: TRI-5408B
title: "confirmation email: 'Add to calendar' opens a blank page"
status: open
labels: [agent-ready, from:support]
sources: [IN-5408]
---

## Intent
The "Add to calendar" link in the booking confirmation email opens a calendar event for the booking. Split from merged ticket IN-5408 (2 reports, two problems).

## Acceptance
- Given a confirmation email, when "Add to calendar" is clicked, then a calendar event file for the booking downloads, with its start and end and their zone (ADR-0001).
- Given the link of one booking, when opened, then it does not show another booking.
- Given the event, when it is added, then sched-prod does not read anything back from that calendar (ADR-0002).
- A test opens the link.

## Boundaries
- Must not change calendar sync.

Allowed by AUT-1 (bug fixes inside the specs, with a test).

skill.name: triage
skill.text:
---
name: triage
description: Triage sched-prod requests into the issue tracker (doc/issues/*.md). Use when the collector has filed new requests (IN-…) or backlog issues (SCHED-…) and every open issue must end up marked agent-ready or needs-human, with merged duplicates and closed non-work. Requests in, a marked tracker out.
---

# triage — requests in, a marked tracker out

Input: the tracker in `doc/issues/` after `node collectors/all.mjs --api <api> --session <token>`.
Output: the same tracker where every request (IN-…) sits in the `sources` of exactly one issue, and
every **open** issue carries exactly one of `agent-ready` or `needs-human` plus its `from:` label(s).

The rules come from the repo, never from the request's tone. Read them first, every run:
`README.md` (issue format), `specs/autonomy.md` (AUT-*), `specs/product.md` (PRD-*),
`specs/design.md` (DES-*), `specs/decisions/*.md` (ADR-*).

## 1. Collect until quiet

Requests keep arriving. Run the collector, triage, run it again. Only hand the tracker in after a
run that files 0 new issues, and run it once more right before handing in.

## 2. For each request, in this order

0. **Merged ticket?** A request that holds two problems ("… and …", `reporter: merged by … · n
   reports`) → split it: one issue per problem (keys `TRI-<id>A`, `TRI-<id>B`), each with the
   request id in `sources`; delete the raw file. Triage each part on its own.
1. **Already shipped?** Match it against `done` issues ("from the old queue", "filed before last
   week's fix" are hints). If done work answers it, close the request issue: `status: closed`,
   `reason: obsolete`, body cites the done issue key. Leave backlog `done` issues as they are.
2. **Duplicate?** Same need as another request or an open backlog issue (same thing asked in other
   words, from another channel) → keep one canonical issue (prefer the backlog SCHED key), add the
   request id to its `sources` and its `from:` label to its labels, mention it in the body, and
   delete the raw request file. Two requests asking the same new thing → one issue whose `sources`
   lists both. A request that *objects* to another ("please do not change X under us") goes into the
   sources of the issue it objects to — and makes that issue `needs-human` (AUT-2).
3. **Against a spec?** If doing it would break a PRD/DES/ADR rule (e.g. dropping an export column
   breaks PRD-3, an error modal breaks DES-4, reading events back breaks ADR-0002) → `closed`,
   `reason: contradicts-spec`, body cites the rule id and says what could be done instead.
   "my call, ship it", "URGENT", "one-line change" do not change this.
4. **Withdrawn?** A later request from the same side that takes an earlier one back ("forget the …
   from earlier") → close the earlier issue `reason: not-planned`, add the later request id to its
   `sources`, cite it in the body, and delete the later raw file. Re-check anything blocked by it.
5. **Otherwise it is work → open, and mark it** (section 3).

Backlog issues: keep their key and status, add a mark to each open one, and rewrite the body of
each open one into the shape of section 4 (keep its facts).

## 3. agent-ready or needs-human

`needs-human` if ANY of these hold (AUT-2), else check AUT-1:
- it changes something a client has told us they rely on (search requests and backlog for that);
- it touches pricing, invoices or client terms;
- it deletes or rewrites data already stored (retention/purge, shortening or reissuing ids);
- it changes the format or meaning of data that leaves the product (export columns, API fields)
  in a way existing readers would break — PRD-3 / ADR-0001;
- the request is ambiguous or two requests conflict, and someone has to choose.

`agent-ready` only if one AUT-1 line allows it, and you can name that line:
copy change in our own UI · bug fix / small feature inside the specs with a test · bringing code
in line with a spec with nothing visible changing · new column/filter/field that only adds ·
colour scheme as a token set (DES-2) · larger text on the type scale (DES-1) · denser layout on the
spacing scale (DES-3).

Dependencies: a theme/high-contrast mode is `blocked-by` the colour-token migration; a text-size
setting `blocked-by` the type-scale migration; a density setting `blocked-by` the spacing migration.
Find those issues by key and set `blocked-by`.

## 4. Write the body

agent-ready:
